steps.title: Distinguish one table from tables
steps.body: сто́л is singular nominative; столы́ is plural nominative. In the selected table sense, the plural refers to tables. The English notes beside these examples are dictionary labels, not plural English translations or complete sentences. Choose the plural form when the question requests plural nominative. Both the ending and the supplied stress matter; do not insert a new stress pattern.

steps.title: Keep lexical gender separate from plural agreement
steps.body: These checks select supplied nominative plural noun forms. Each noun retains its dictionary gender; plural adjective agreement does not require separate masculine, feminine and neuter plural endings. The source’s single plural agreement category is not a claim that nouns lose lexical gender. Gender alone is not a complete algorithm for unfamiliar plural endings or stress. Learn these supplied pairs rather than applying them to every noun.

steps.title: Recognize the town pair
steps.body: го́род is singular nominative; города́ is plural nominative in this supplied pair. Select the latter for towns. The plural ending differs from the table pair and its supplied stress is on the final syllable. These patterns are word-specific recognition evidence, not permission to generate an unlisted form.

steps.title: Recognize the book pair and its spelling
steps.body: кни́га is singular nominative; кни́ги is plural nominative. Select the latter for books. The supplied plural retains its stress. Its final vowel follows the stem’s last consonant, one of the seven spelling-rule letters taught in the later spelling session. This same correct book pair is reused there as reinforcement; earlier independent credit does not replace that later objective’s checks.

steps.title: Recognize the window pair and shifted stress
steps.body: окно́ is singular nominative; о́кна is plural nominative in the supplied dictionary pair. Select the latter for windows. Notice the supplied stress moves to the first syllable. An ending-only guess would lose part of the taught form; do not invent another accent or treat this pair as every neuter noun’s algorithm.

steps.title: Recognize the mom pair
steps.body: ма́ма is singular nominative; ма́мы is plural nominative. Select the latter for moms in the supplied sense. The ending changes while the supplied stress stays in place. A feminine dictionary label alone does not prove every feminine noun has this ending.

steps.title: Recognize the house pair
steps.body: до́м is singular nominative; дома́ is plural nominative in the supplied house sense. Select the latter for houses. Preserve the source stress shift. The dictionary’s English house/home labels identify a sense; they are not a plural translation of the Russian form.

sessions.title: Recognize nominative forms and plural spelling

steps.title: Singular and plural forms
steps.body: Adjectives agree with their nouns in gender, number and case. In хорошее письмо, the adjective describes a neuter singular noun. хоро́ший is the dictionary form: masculine singular nominative. This lesson compares singular and plural nominative forms, then explains the spelling in the retained plurals.

steps.title: The seven-letter spelling rule
steps.body: After г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, or щ, write и rather than ы. The seven-letter condition is required. This rule applies to the spelling of noun and adjective endings. In кни́ги, и follows г; in хоро́шие, и follows ш. The rule controls spelling, but the question determines the required gender, number and case.

steps.title: A worked noun plural
steps.body: For these nominative checks, кни́га means book in the singular and кни́ги means books in the plural. To form this plural, replace the singular ending with the plural ending: кни́га becomes кни́ги. The stem ends in г, so the seven-letter rule requires и. To return to singular nominative, choose кни́га.

steps.title: Two plural forms, different patterns
steps.body: кни́ги is plural nominative in this lesson. дни is also plural nominative and means days. Its и does not follow a letter in the seven-letter set, so дни is not an example of that spelling replacement. Not every plural ending in и comes from the seven-letter rule. Identify number from the requested form and context.

steps.title: Adjective number and dictionary form
steps.body: хоро́шее is neuter singular nominative; хоро́шие is plural nominative. To change the neuter singular form to plural nominative, choose хоро́шие; to return to neuter singular, choose хоро́шее. For the masculine singular dictionary form, choose хоро́ший. All these options are correctly spelled: the questions test form recognition rather than choosing between correct and incorrect spellings.

sessions.title: Choose the admitted plural agreement form

steps.title: Recognize the supplied plural modifiers
steps.body: синие книги — the dark blue books. Наши — Our. These supplied examples introduce plural modifiers or plural referents. This lesson asks you to recognize the listed form pairs; it does not demonstrate producing agreement for every noun or case.

steps.title: Read the adjective with its noun
steps.body: In the retained nominative example синие книги — the dark blue books, the adjective modifies a plural noun. The complete phrase provides the plural reading here; do not infer a universal noun-case interpretation from an isolated spelling.

steps.title: Compare the possessive forms
steps.body: мо́й and мои́ both retain the meaning my. In the supplied fields, мо́й is masculine singular nominative and мои́ is plural nominative. The requested plural is a number distinction, not a different owner or a change of English meaning.

steps.title: Work the guided adjective pair
steps.body: но́вый and но́вые both mean new. The supplied masculine singular nominative form is но́вый; the plural nominative is но́вые. Guided practice uses this pair. Recognize the whole form and requested number; this does not establish every case ending.

steps.title: Compare the demonstrative forms
steps.body: The dictionary groups э́та and э́ти under the same demonstrative entry labelled this. In ordinary English the plural demonstrative reading is these. The supplied feminine singular nominative form is э́та; the plural nominative form is э́ти. The plural does not have a feminine-only gender. Distinguish the source entry label from the number-sensitive English reading.

steps.title: Apply the distinction to a different adjective
steps.body: The retained nominative section supplies синий as the masculine singular form and синие in синие книги as the plural form of the same dark-blue adjective. This source prints these words without written stress; no stress mark is inserted. The independent adjective check uses this different lexeme and ending shape from the guided new/new-plural pair. Choose the supplied plural rather than repeat its singular form. These examples are bounded nominative recognition, not a rule that every adjective or every word with similar final letters changes identically.

sessions.title: Choose between the admitted existence and absence lines

steps.title: Presence and the nominative
steps.body: Use the presence construction when the line says that something exists. In these supplied examples, the noun naming what exists is nominative. Read the Russian line and identify whether it states presence. На э́той у́лице есть францу́зы — There are Frenchmen on this street. В Москве́ есть ста́рые зда́ния — There are old buildings in Moscow.

steps.title: Absence and the genitive
steps.body: Use the absence construction when the line says that something does not exist. In these supplied examples, the absence word is followed by a genitive noun. Presence and absence require different case explanations.

steps.title: Compare the complete examples
steps.body: Compare the positive and negative lines below. For a positive line choose the nominative presence explanation; for a negative line choose the genitive absence explanation. Нет рестора́нов — There are no restaurants. В Москве́ нет ста́рых зда́ний — There are no old buildings in Moscow.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Read the whole shown line, then choose the complete case explanation. A missed check returns to all teaching and examples.
